newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower on falling cash prices.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower on falling cash prices.

text.p: CME live cattle futures retreated late to settle lower after trading mixed much of the day as concerns over cash cattle prices weighed on trade sentiment, floor sources said.
Feeder cattle futures followed, with higher corn futures also adding to pressure, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.475 to 0.100 cent per lb lower with June off 0.350 at 63.775 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.550 to 0.100 lower with August off most at 76.750 cents.

June live cattle eased to its lowest level in nearly six weeks as boxed beef prices again slipped and amid ideas fed cattle markets could ease again next week. But losses were limited by expectations markets were close to bottoming, traders said.
"The market is trying to find our seasonal low, a trader said.
Sellers cited falling wholesale beef values and expectations that packers may only pay $63 per cwt for fed cattle next week as selling factors.

Buyers cited recent active boxed beef sales, record feedlot cattle sales in Kansas this week and long-term support that developed in the past in the 63.000- to 64.000-cent area. Also, the longer-term outlook is for feedlot numbers to decline.
Cargill Investor Services, E.D.&F. Man and FIMAT Futures USA sold June while Cargill, E.D.&F. Man and Prudential Securities sold August, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses again liquidated June positions by selling the June 64 straddle. They also bought June 63 puts. Commercial hedging continued in October, buying puts and selling calls, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle and pork complex futures by moving lower later in the session, with higher corn futures adding to selling pressure. Feeders had traded unevenly early as cash ideas were mixed, traders said.
Current plentiful cattle supplies on feed should suppress demand for feeders. But tight feeder supplies will persist into the fall which lent some support, sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index dipped $0.14 to $77.60 per cwt after recently notching 33-month highs.
Stone Traders sold August into sell stops late with local buying limiting the setback. Smith Barney sold October. RBH and LFG bought early while Prudential Securities sold, pit sources said.
